Kalyth is the last survivor of an Elan tribe. She had a husband and three children. She’s spent months running through Ampelas Rooted, a K’Chain Che’Malle nest of the last Matron, Gunth’an Acyl
Kalyth is summoned and runs through tunnels of machinery, oil, cables, and ramps through chambers called Feed, Womb, Heart, and Eyes
The nest is populated by J’an Sentinels, K’ell Hunters, and Ve’Gath soldiers with ornate grilled visors and jaws with ghastly grins

At the landing before the Matron’s room is Bre’nigan, a thousand year old J’an Sentinel with aged silver scales and a magenta-hued silver curved sword slung through a brass ring embedded in its scales at its hip. The sword is as tall as Kalyth
In the nest, Matron Gunth’an Acyl speaks to Kalyth in her mind.
Kalyth is her Destriant because humans rule the world, she sends her away on an impossible quest to find her a Mortal Sword and Shield Anvil before the enemy finds her along with others
K’ell Hunter Sag’churok
K’ell Hunter Rythok
K’ell Hunter Kor Thuran
One Daughter Gunth Mach, the only child that can potentially breed
Shi’gal Assassin Gu’Rull

Matrons can only produce three Shi’gal assassins at a time. They all defend the Matron whenever one Shi’Gal assassin wants to kill the matron. The fact that Matron Acyl is sending one away shows her desperation
Shi’gal Gu’Rull stands on the edge of Brow at night
He’s the eldest Shi’gal Assassin at 6100 years, is twice the height of a K’ell Hunter, and has defeated 7 Shi’gal assassins in his life
K’ell hunters were created with lifespans of 1,000 years. Shi’gal assassins could potentially outlive the Matron
Gu’Rull doesn’t have faith in Kalyth or humans, reflects on Redmask’s failure
Gu’Rull smells death from the east winds. The west Awl’dan yielded failure. The north is a lifeless realm of ice and sea. Their only direction remaining is south
Shi’gal assassins have not left the KCCM keep in 800 years, decides to scout ahead
The matron had granted Gu’Rull new body parts in the past month. Feathery wings, two new eyes under his jaw

An unnamed figure travels with a group of seven including Sheb, Last, Nappet, Asane, Breath, Taxilian, Rautos
Traversing through hills and ridges, no trees, populated by scaled rodents, big rhizan, and cape moths
(Cape Moths)
Cape Moths above follow the unnamed figure. The figure has dusty green skin and has tusks, is alone, and speaks to himself in seven voices
Heboric sees visions before him
A stub-tailed bipedal lizard wearing black armor stands on a stone platform looking up at a crucified dragon. Spiked to a lattice of wooden beams, bleeding into the gutters

Two wolves on a grassy ridge watch Heboric, heavy rain clouds behind them. Heboric turns away to walk towards statues with cowls, facing away from Heboric, standing on glittering ground. As he gets closer to the statue, he is wrapped in cold shadow
Heboric sees swirls of stars above floating down like snow melting on him. Below, more swirls of stars and a dozen jade suns approaching Heboric.
Heboric recognizes the star pattern of Fener below. Both Heboric and Fener are in the jade suns’ path, no way to stop it. The god and priest of war has doomed the world and the Abyss gives answer.
The final war has begun

Behold, my friends, I am justice. And when at last we meet, you will not like it. And if irony awakens in you at the end, see me weep with these tears of jade, and answer with a smile. If you’ve the courage. Have you, my friends, the courage?
(Deadhouse Gates)

On the otataral island desert, Heboric touched a giant jade hand which infected his stump. When Baudin pressed the infected stump to the Fener tattoo on his heart, it pulled Fener into the mortal realm. Heboric also obtained two ghostly hands: the left outlined in Fener tattoos, the right with veins of otataral red and jade green
(Memories of Ice)
While Anomander Rake and Whiskeyjack were talking about the Crippled God, they also talked about Fener and Heboric
Heboric was an imperial historian that investigated Empress Laseen’s involvement in the assassination of Kellanved and Dancer

Fener’s Reve was a ritual performed by a high ranking servant of Fener to judge someone that had betrayed Fener or his servants. The condemned person would have their hands severed and sent to Fener. Fener would then claim the hands, and thus pieces of their soul
Laseen ordered the Claw to orchestrate a false Fener’s Reve upon Heboric as punishment
Fener couldn’t touch Heboric’s hands because it was an unjust Reve, had to tattoo Heboric’s body to seal them for the time
Fener planned to wait until Heboric died, so that he could receive Heboric’s soul and have him become a vengeful spirit that brought justice to the corrupt Fener priests, the Claw, and the Empress
HOWEVER, the plan got derailed when Heboric touched the jade giant, Heboric’s tattoos unsealed and the power went through to Heboric’s severed arms.
The jade power then expelled Fener from his realm and pulled him into the mortal realm making him vulnerable.

It is around this time that Treach dies on Genabackis after being mauled by four undead K’Chain Che’Malle and ascended to Trake, the new god of war, when the Elder God K’rul assembles a pantheon to face the Crippled God
(House of Chains)
The jade power inside Heboric was defeating the otataral half
L’oric tells Heboric that the first jade giant was found in the otataral mines. The jade giants are alien intruders, expected and chained in otataral
A female scholar suggested otataral was created when sorcery had drained or annihilated all energy around it - like slag with the ore burned out (slag being the melted rock to harvest the raw ore)
A power that gods do not have, but two events might fit the criteria: The Ritual of Tellann and the calling down of the Crippled God
L’oric noted ‘Together, there at the ends of [Heboric’s] wrists, they became the weight of the world’
Felisin Sha’ik wanted to send Heboric back to the jade giant on otataral island to learn more about the jade giant and a way to defeat Adjunct Tavore’s otataral sword
Heboric is deep in sleep induced by the hen‘bara tea
Heboric floats in a sea of stars, having an existential crisis as he realizes each star is a sun with their own worlds, he asks himself if those are warrens
Hundreds of giant jade statues, naked, some were whole and some were shattered with the pieces trailing behind
The statues were naked, immaculately human with the faintest expression of resignation
In each statue held thousands of humans wailing in pain and terror
The humans try to talk to Heboric, they had killed their gods by indifference and their intelligence
Gods were born of belief and belief is dead
‘It’s not the gods that are important, it is the stepping stone outside of oneself that gift a mortal with virtue - compassion’
The giant statues all originated from one point in the sea, all floating one by one towards a red wound with tendrils of grey storms of chains, big enough to swallow hundreds of thousands of worlds
Heboric wakes in his tent
Otataral no longer present in his ghost hands, instead black liquid stripes floating on his ghostly arms resembling a tiger
His senses like smell, hearing, and vision acutely sharpened. He also gains darkvision
Treach, the Tiger of Summer, has made Heboric his Destriant
‘No gifts were truly clean in the giving’
After the Battle of Raraku, Heboric’s desire to revisit the jade statue remained
(Bonehunters)
Heboric receives whispers and dreams by jade strangers that make him go to the Jade Statue in Otataral Island
Crokus Younghand was tasked by Cotillion to defend Heboric, Scillara, and Felisin Younger on their way
They are attacked by the Unbound T’lan Imass to prevent Heboric from reaching the Jade Statue and kidnap Felisin Younger

An event similar to the Fall of the Crippled God occurs, Ganoes Paran made a deal with Hood for his help, resulting in reviving Heboric. Heboric’s proximity to the Jade Statue triggers huge jade arms and domes to protect the world from the falling suns.

i.html: (Midnight Tides) Yan Tovis is introduced as the Atri-Preda of Fent Reach. She immediately surrendered without a fight when the Tiste Edur first invaded.

(Bonehunters) She was assigned to Preda Tomad Sengar’s 3rd Imperial Fleet to harass the north coast of Seven Cities to find challengers to Rhulad, liberate subjugated Edur tribes like Sepik, and massacre their oppressors. Taralack Veed had to convince Yan Tovis that Icarium is a worthy challenger.
She was present when Tomad’s fleet attacked the Malaz 14th Army fleet and he recognized the Edur ship Silanda.

(Reaper’s Gale) Yan Tovis arrived safely to Letheras, but her captain Varat Taun was traumatized after witnessing Icarium’s rage. Senior Assessor used his High Denul magic to try and heal the trauma. After Icarium was delivered, Yan Tovis took Varat Taun and Senior Assessor out of the city to be away from Icarium.

Once Yan Tovis arrives at Boaral Keep, she meets the witches Pully & Skwish who cursed the Boaral Family - who slaughtered Shake - by making all the men kill their wives. The witches reveal that (a) Tiste Edur’s demon spirit-god had killed Yan Tovis’ mother, the Queen of the Shake whom Yan Tovis had not seen in 10 years, and (b) Princess Yan Tovis is now betrothed to Shake Brullyg of Second Maiden Fort. Yan Tovis meets her half-brother Yedan Derryg for the first time, working as the master of arms. Together, they witnessed the Bonehunters burn
their ships off the coast. ‘The Malazans are on our shore.’

They travel to Road’s End village where the Shoulderfolk of the Old Ways (Shake coven of witches and warlocks) including Pully & Skwish met. Yan Tovis believed that the last Rise (title for Shake King) Teyan Atovis had drank himself to death after accumulating so much Letherii debt. To the coven’s anger, Yan Tovis refuses to get married, renounces the Old Ways their leadership of the Shake.

cards.h: ** Yan Tovis, Yedan Derryg, and the Shake

i.html: (Reaper’s Gale) Yan Tovis and Yedan Derryg go to Second Maiden Fort by the time the Bonehunters occupied Shake Brullyg’s estate and meets the Malazans. Tavore recognized that the Shake appeared to be refugees. Deadsmell had spoken to Sandalath Drukorlat and recognized the Shake titles
Twilight, Rise, Watch. All guarding the Shores of Night.
The Shake’s blood had been thinned over generations, and have forgotten a lot of their original history
In the Shake language
Yenander means twilight
Antovis means night or dark
Yedanas means watch
The Shake watch the Shore where the newborn K’Chain Che’Malle come from
After the Bonehunters sail away, Second Maiden Fort is full of ex-prisoners now free, indebted and murderers.

cards.h: ** Yan Tovis, Yedan Derryg, and the Shake

i.html: The Shake believes the world started as nothing but sea, and inevitably the sea will rise and devour all
The Shake witnessed from their homeland, the Isle (transformed into the prison island Second Maiden Fort). The shore was their metaphor of land vs. sea
The Isle used to be connected to the main lands with land bridges, all have sunken now
Some Shake newborns were born grotesque with monstrous features
Taloned hands and feet, scaled elongated face, a tail, and lurid green eyes
The coven of Shake Witches would choose some, the rest of the children would be sacrificed to the sea

Something very strange and not further explained, demons engaged in war concerned about their species’ survival dumped their seed into the ocean which ends up washing onto shore, clinging on any living thing, maybe even hijacking a baby in the womb giving the Shake babies the demonic features

[Maybe there was enough evidence in Reaper’s Gale, probably even all the way back to Midnight Tide’s prologue, at this point we can surmise that the K’Chain Che’Malle were the original inhabitants of the Lether continent. A Matron’s genetic material is the reason why generations of Shake have taken on lizard-like features.]
Yan Tovis left the Shake because of the sacrificing of babies too demonic, the witches and warlocks having controlled the Shake taking power, and belief from the Shore
The Shake people were viewed with disgust by the Nerek, Tarthenal, Faered, and Letherii
Yan Tovis had chosen each person in her company because of their Shake ancestry, however diluted it may be
The Bonehunters
The Shake
Pully looks down into a pit of writhing snakes, laments her aging body, pops a squat and pisses
Skwish emerges from the snake pit, she travelled far to take a look. Things to the east are cold and bad as they predicted.
Black clouds and green lights in the starless sky. Dust of bone, skin, dreams, and surprise
Pully and Skwish plan to banish Yan Tovis and Yedan Derryg from the Shake next time Yan Tovis talks about marching away from the Shore
They walk back to the village not knowing they’re the last Shake witches
Udinaas and Onrack wait outside as Silchas and Rud Elalle speak inside a hut
Rud Ellale is innocent, but eventually the Eleint blood will awaken an innate megalomania, an obsession for power
Silchas knows few people that overcame their Eleint nature: Anomander Rake, maybe Osserc, a bonecaster, and a soletaken Jaghut
Silchas has hope for Rud Elalle because he is third generation and opposed his mother’s will
Onrack doesn’t understand why Udinaas would give his son away
Udinaas knows he can’t go against nature or instinct [of the eleint]
Udinaas does not tell him that he’s sending Rud Elalle away to save the Refugium, and the Imass who would accept their annihilation without hesitation to save Rud Elalle
Rud Elalle and Silchas step out of the tent
Udinaas and Onrack together walks towards them as Onrack weeps
Tanakalian and Krughava disembarked and walk to the Bolkando delegation tent
Krughava reminds Tanakalian of heroes from the childhood stories and legends his grandfather told him
Krughava is in her 50’s, iron hair color, winter skies eye color, face like a carved cliff face
Tanakalian did not tell her of Run’Thurvian’s warning. He only gave news of his death, made Krughava distressed
Ahead, the Bolkando sentries were looking at row upon row of enormous lizards stalking by the shore
Inside the Bolkando delegation tent is Chancellor Rava, King Tarkulf, and Conquestor Avalt
Per custom, Tanakalian and Krughava are served three drinks
The blood of the king’s 14th daughter, sacrificed to show his commitment to the delegation
Nectar of sharada flowers from the Royal Garden, fertilized by seven generations of the royal stillbirths
Allegedly regular spring water
(Chancellor Rava)
Chancellor Rava and Conquestor Avalt discuss after the Grey Helms leave the delegation camp
The Bolkando servants had their tongues cut out and eardrums punctured to prevent communication from any spies
They plan to give them whatever they need in their futile venture east, send a salvager to follow them, and any survivors that return would be castrated and sold as slaves to the D’rhresh
The Khundryl Burned Tears had visited Bolkando before
King Tarkulf had liked them and led his own armies, which troubled the Chancellor and Conquestor who have been manipulating him
The Bolkando buried corpses and carrion birds in the swamps so that the Khundryl Burned Tear camps in the marshes would die from fever
The blood and stillborn juice was a colorful lie, the Grey Helms were given Belt Juice that will show in their scars
Rava chose Lady Felash who spurned his advances, and his spies were tortured to death. Rava accepts the loss and pulls out
(Bolkando Servants)
Turns out the servants are spies and they used blinking morse codes to communicate and send messages back to Lady Felash, she holds grudges
Life in Bolkando is an adventure
Yan Tovis yells at Skwish & Pully to stop pissing and spitting, rejecting their demands for a king
As prophesied, the water levels are rising, shores are drowning, and kin has slaughtered kin.
Yan Tovis plans to go to Third Maiden Isle and free the prisoners to save them from the rising water level
Then she will lead her people away the shore
A bone white dragon [Silchas Ruin] and burning gold dragon [Rud Elalle] circle the Imass camp
Two figures cane to watch them [Note: Probably Udinaas and Onrack]
An emlava celebrates their first kill
: Joshua Butler

The Snake
The Bonehunters
Perish Grey Helms

Ruthan tells her not to tie her straps too tight, fashion is a means of emasculating and imprisoning women’s freedom
Shurq responds it’s self imposed and women are inherently competitive and misogynistic
Ruthan is worried about the Deck reading and warns Shurq to stay away

Shurq tells him to speak to King Tehol Beddict or any of his other friends of high rank and agrees to sleep with him as long as he doesn’t get jealous
Kisswhere rides to Letheras and reflects
Her sister Sgt. Sinter is loyal to Kisswhere’s capriciousness, to a fault
Kisswhere has slept with a married man and escaped by signing up to 10 years service to the Malazan military, planned to desert if she got bored
Sinter, loyal to her sister in all things, followed her. She was talented and worked her way up to sergeant
Badan Gruk fell in love with Sinter, possible that Sinter reciprocates
Kisswhere feels guilty for their fate and wished she’d died in captivity or took Tavore’s offer of discharge back in Malaz City after the outlawing of the Bonehunters
Sinter, however, became loyal to Tavore. Kisswhere hates Tavore for stealing her sister
Sinter senses something is wrong, asks where Nep Furrow is, and says they have to hurry
Fist Keneb and Fist Blistig drink at upscale tavern
Blistig disapproves of Fist Arbin spending time close with his heavies
Keneb feels he didn’t belong at the last Reading, was only there for his son Grub.
The last reading gave Adjunct Tavore the will to do everything that came after, including the Malaz City incident and Kalam’s ‘murder’
Deadsmell paid a month’s wages for a seat on the fourth floor with roof access and a view of the Grand Lecture Medix
Masan Gilani, Ebron, Cpl. Shard, Sgt. Cord, Limp, and (uninvited) Crump enter with food and drinks
Crump plans to carve driftwood he has, he’s ordered to carve the everyone in the room galloping over flames except Deadsmell
Deadsmell pulls out dead animals and lines them up to perform a ritual that keeps Hood out of the room
A bird, rat, iguana, and fox-sized bat thing
The iguana eye blinks, High House Death has arrived
Sgt. Hellian is drunk and wants to stop the twins Cpl. Touchy and Brethless from hiring prostitutes
Sgt. Urb has to lead her, Skulldeath who is smitten with Hellian follows from behind
Inside the expensive looking brothel that makes Urb want to empty his wallet, they find Touchy and Brethless with a skinny prostitute and a fat prostitute
The skinny one charges with a knife but Urb chops his hand on her wrist, disarming her. The fat one charges with a chair but gets shoved down
Six guards appear
Brys watches the Malazans assemble and has opinions

(1) Adjunct Tavore has no social graces, is awkward and clumsy, appears consistently distracted by an insurmountable obstacle. Despite this her soldiers are undeniably loyal. No eye rolls or staring daggers
(2) Quick Ben, a name lacking in respect for a Ceda
(3) Fiddler
(4) Hedge

Tavore says it must happen even if it’s a mistake, addresses Stormy as Adjutant even though he’s been a sergeant for awhile now. To face an ambush, it must be sprung
Fiddler says he can do it, the problem is uninvited guests. Brys’ spidey sense goes out but it’s too late
Three cards are played on the table, the Reading has begun

Outside the Grand Lecture Medix, the Errant feels like he’s pummeled by invisible fists and tastes blood in his mouth

Ursto Hoobutt, Pinosel, and Bugg stand between the vast power of the Deck reading and Seren’s son
Ursto and Pinosel burst into flames and melt. Bugg sweats profusely
Bugg says this is no ordinary caster of the Tiles
(Deadsmell)

The rat falls upward to the ceiling, intestines dangling
The blue fox-turtle bat thing bites off the iguana tail
The iguana runs into the window trying to get out
The bird flies around the room and explodes into feathers, crashing into the post, wine bottles explode
Crump’s horse-riding carvings become animate and ride on the floor
Ebron vomits, Limp slips on the wine and shatters his knee, Deadsmell crawls to a corner, Masan Gilani crawls under the bed

Two dragons burst from the inn, completely destroying it and sending people flying 50 paces. No survivors

Hellian elbows a bearded man as a wall collapses on everyone in the brothel room
Urb pulls Hellian to get out of there

The Errant enters and builds magical power
Fiddler says the Master of the Deck has awakened and can appear to face him
Brys says he has lived in stone with the names of forgotten gods written on him, he is enough to stop him
The Errant flees
Fiddler understands the Adjunct now, the enemy has been found
No one in the room was claimed, they are marked
Fiddler can see the end, apologizes to Tavore for what will happen
Fiddler and Brys laugh, both of them had bluffed against the Errant

The Errant is shaken
Does not want to face the Master of the Deck. Wants to kill Brys, recalls the pleasure in killing Feather Witch.
Afraid of Fiddler because he wields power but has no ambition to exploit. Only wants to be left alone
Seren’s son was protected by Ursto, Pinosel, Mael, and Kilava’s presence which he didn’t recognize but was enough to discourage him
Potential allies with Banaschar, Fener, and forces to the far east
(Telorast & Curdle)
Telorast & Curdle fly off in their dragon forms, Telorast scooped up and ate a street merchant, and settled into their lizard skeleton forms on a hilltop leagues north of Letheras
They consider killing the man that keeps the throne empty and sows chaos [the Errant]
Everyone is their enemy, they want to tear everything apart and for Curdle to not mess it up like last time
Telorast sees green “blobs” in the sky
(Withal)
Withal dotes on his wife Sandalath after she comes home from the Deck reading
Sandalath claims the past of High House Dark is dead, the thrones abandoned, no king or queen, and doesn’t make sense for Quick Ben, a human, to be the Magus of Dark
(Deadsmell)
The iguana bit Limp’s ear, Crump warns against letting Deadsmell the necromancer heal wounds
Ebron tells Cpl. Shard that all the warrens opened during the Deck reading
Deadsmell says Sinn is in the middle of it, and Shard’s squad might be her escort again
Everyone runs away. Brys, Tavore, and Lostara remain in the room
Lostara looks like she’s barely holding back the sorrow she’s been holding inside her
Tavore thanks Brys for his presence against the Errant, heard he was resurrected
Brys didn’t like the feeling of being manipulated and that his soul was out of his control
Tavore says her brother is Master of the Deck, but they are not allies

Sometimes, Brys ventured, when nothing can be shared except regret, then regret must serve as a place to begin. Reconciliation does not demand that one side surrender to the other. The simple, mutual recognition that mortuaries were made is in itself a closing of the divide
Brys asks if her brother knows her predicament
Tavore is alert and says she never mentioned a predicament. Brys panics thinking he said too much
Tavore plans to gather her allies and march east through the Wastelands
Brys discourages it, the lands east of the Wastelands do not sound promising
Tavore is not looking for promises
Quick Ben sits on a rooftop, bothered that he’s Magus of Dark. Needs to stay away from Sandalath
Sgt. Fiddler, Sgt. Gesler, and Cpl. Stormy sing old Napan pirate songs
Bottle’s looking for a healer for his broken ribs
Grub and Sinn ran away
Hedge approaches to ask why he’s Mason of Death
Hedge “is needed to build them a road”
Something happens in the city that catches Quick Ben’s attention
Brys Beddict is attacked by the Errant, grey tendrils constrict and choke Brys
The Errant taunts that he nudged Brys to drink the poisoned wine, but now takes direct action
Ublala Pung punches the Errant knocking him away. Brys is freed. Ublala forgot what question he was supposed to ask Tehol and Brys
Sgt. Sinter arrives with Sgt. Badan Gruk’s squad. She came to save Brys, but falls unconscious as soon as she dismounts
The squad entered the alley, but the Errant escaped
Sgt. Badan Gruk provides Brys’ escort to the palace
(Quick Ben)
Quick Ben senses the Toblakai in Ublala, but is more interested in the Dal Honese woman, Sgt. Sinter
(Fiddler)

A second card. Chain, unaligned. It was too strong, chains reaching into the heart of the Bonehunters. Unclear who is pulling who

The wrong proportion of herbs can kill her or make her insane
The K’Chain Che’Malle set up a camp for her comfort, but she doesn’t want it
Shi’Gal Gu’Rull circles in the sky

K’ell Rythok and K’ell Kor Thuran sense Sag’Churok’s oil and get ready

Sag’Churok and Gunth Mach privately speak
The others aren’t aware she is the matron’s daughter, but just as a drone
Shi’gal Gu’Rull unintentionally leak to Gunth Mach. The assassin respects Sag’Churok and Gunth Mach because they have battle experience, the other two K’ell Hunters do not
The K’Chain Che’Malle are one of the four Founding Races. They are very intelligent dinosaurs that developed technology and whose Kaschan warren manipulated gravity
The K’Chain Che’Malle ruled the Letherii continent. When Scabandari Bloodeye shattered Kurald Emurlahn, he led his people to invade and seek refuge in the mortal world and slaughtered the KCCM

Passed down through every generation of the Sengar women, the K’Chain Che’Malle performed a Kaschan Ritual as vengeance against the Tiste, turning Mother Dark into a black hole and set up the heat death of the universe
The last KCCM city was Morn (Southern Genabackis), where the ‘Short-Tails’ were about to rebel

In Kallor’s Empire, his researchers studied ancient barrows and constructs. KCCM Matrons came together to resurrect the primitive Short-Tailed ancestors, but they refused to work together and engaged in civil war which led to the destruction of their race
As a consequence, a rent that led to Chaos was opened and a Matron sacrificed herself to seal it
The Pannion Domin had read in Gothos’ Folly that the K’Chain Nah’ruk, the Short-Tails, were the ones that created the flying fortress, and believes Moon’s Spawn is a K’Chain Nah’ruk skykeep

Kilava Onass, an Imass and sister to Onos T’oolan, attempted to save two Jaghut children from her peoples’ genocide by placing them in a rent that she thought was Omtose Phellack, the Elder warren of the Jaghut
One of the Jaghut children grew up to be the Pannion Seer
Instead, the rent led to Chaos that opened during the civil war between the KCCM and KCNR
The KCCM Matron resurrected KCCM from their tombs as undead, but turned her insane of which the Pannion Seer took advantage and controlled the Matron
K’ell Hunters are specifically the warriors of KCCM with the swords for arms

Heboric says tribes from all continents share the fact that they all are doomed to go extinct
There’s various ways to come to where Heboric is, chewing herbs becomes ritual
Heboric pulls his hands out, rust red, and puts his hands back in the sand

The light of the jade streaks illuminate them

Claws slick with neural poison kills them all, two scouts flee to alert their people

Sag’Churok can sense the inexperienced K’ell hunters struggled against their Nectar of Slaying, something like adrenaline

Sag’Churok forces his sleeping glands to suppress them adrenaline
Soon they will venture east, Sag’Churok expects the K’ell will kill humans before then

Gu’Rull kills the real scouts

There existed dogs that followed KCCM “Furies”
Gu’Rull learned previously that his new wings absorb too much heat, overheats in the daytime. The cool night air helps maintain balance

The scene changes to a plain burning KCCM mechanisms, armies on the horizon, large shadows covering the land and converging
The shadows swarm to a single point as if plunging through a gate
Twin suns then blind her and burn her
(Kalyth)
Kalyth wakes up, Sag’Churok stands beside looking at her
Gunth Mach cooks meat by the campfire
Kalyth is tired of meat all the time, never seen them eat vegetables or their bread with mushroom like texture
Stavi and Storii are twin sisters, stalking their adopted father Tool knowing they can get whatever they want from him
Their mother Hetan stops their mischief and chases them off to protect Tool
They get their “sly gift” of manipulation from their biological father, Kruppe
Onos Toolan is the warchief of the White Face Barghast. He summons the clan chiefs
A third of the clans ignored it, mostly from the south. Rumors that most of them mutinied and wandered into the Saphinaud and Bolkando kingdoms to find work at bodyguards
The Gadra, lead by chief Stolmen, found a herd of bhederin to live off of. Tool didn’t feel he was disloyal

The shoulder-seers prophesied that the Barghast would fight a war of vengeance against ancient Tiste Edur that had preyed upon the Barghast generations ago
The Barghast sold everything to purchase tamales and grain and follow the seers through warrens to reach the Lether continent
However, they found Tiste Edur and Letherii. Both peoples that were crushed and terrorized by the Lether Empire. To war against them would be unjust
Hetan’s brother Cafal has spent months trying to meld the clans together but is failing
Tool was able to hold back the Barghast from attacking the Lether Empire until the day he witnessed Toc’s death. Then the Barghast were unleashed
Kilava seeing Tool’s grief reminded her of love and friendship, so she left to seek her own [with Onrack]
Hetan misses her sister-in-law but wants to slap her for abandoning Tool in his grief

Tool jokes that it was easier along the Imass. Hetan mocks them for their insanity and asks why didn’t they just face their own mistake and injustice hunting the Jaghut. Tool says she shouldn’t ask that question, the T’lan Imass might not be able to handle that all they have are mistakes

The Barghast and the Moranth are descendants of the Imass that did not partake in the Ritual of Tellann. The Barghast had sailed to Genabackis to continue the genocide of the Jaghut, and settled in present-day Capustan. They buried their dugout canoes and made the First Landing a site for their pilgrimage as they migrated to the Barghast Range. However, Daru and Capu settlers claimed the land for themselves, destroyed the Barghast barrows, and expelled the Barghast.
After a long period of time, the Barghast lost their seafaring skills and historical origins.

Hetan and Cafal Taur came to Capustan to demand the return of their ancient remains of their ancestors and free the Barghast spirit-gods to reunite the Barghast clans. After the events of Memories of Ice, Silverfox had freed and revived Tool as a mortal man. Tool and Kilava head to
(Memories of Ice)

Talamandas is an acorn sticksnare who used to be of the First Hearth of the Knotted Barghast Clan. When Quick Ben freed him, Talamandas became his buddy for all of Memories of Ice, even helping him pin the Pannion Seer down in the climax
He revealed to Quick Ben that the Barghast were descended from Imass that did not partake in the Ritual of Tellann and came to Genabackis on dugout canoes to chase Jaghut.
He wanted to free the First Families, spirits worshiped by the Barghast, and the dugout canoes preserved by magic in the Barghast barrow grounds that Capustan had settled on top of.
Talamandas’ power drew on Hood’s power, the Barghast gods let the Barghast be servants of Hood.
Torrent is the last Awl leader
He led the surviving Awl children to join the Gadra Barghast clan where they were absorbed
Torrent knew he would be the last Awl leader, the children assimilated Barghast culture and no longer spoke Awl
Torrent accepted the fact that the Awl culture will die out
Torrent was scared of the Barghast women pursuing him, still a virgin he fled leagues away from the Gadra camp
Torrent has a nightmare that Toc’s corpse was haunting and chasing him, then wakes up in a cold sweat
Six Barghast dogs approach Torrent, he decides to investigate a circle of birds to the north. Two dogs follow while four continue back to camp
Torrent reflects that if the Awl would not have followed Redmask if they were content and weren’t desperate to escape genocide by the Lether Empire.
The Awl should’ve surrendered to the Letherii, Redmask’s beliefs were suicide for the Awl
Torrent believes all people were doomed against civilization. Akrynnai traders set up camps at the Barghast orders and D’rhasilhani horse sellers try to entice Barghast warriors with their herds
Torrent finds the 28 scout corpses and finds out they all died against a single beast
Torrent wonders of their quarry was a plains bear that hasn’t been seen in 7 generations
Torrent decides to report back to the Barghast chiefs and let them deal with it
Setoc is a girl raised by wolves, living along the Barghast while her wolf family stays close by
Formerly Stayandi, a Letherii girl whose family was slaughtered by Redmask after he took over the Renfayar Awl clan and before confronting Hadralt (Ganetok Awl leader)

The Barghast propagate a legend surrounding her, that she is spirit blessed with holy protection by the wolves, holder of a thousand hearts. The Barghast leave her wolf family alone and even the Akrynnai knows her story
Setoc watches the four Barghast dogs return after the KCCM slaughtered the scouts
Cafal, the “Great Warlock” and “Finder of the Barghast Gods” [Note: Hetan’s brother], came to speak to Setoc and examine her soul
The wolves howled, believing Setoc to be at the heart of a celestial conflagration, and want to sacrifice themselves so that Setoc can be spared
Setoc wants to tell Cafal that the Gadra and other Barghast clans are doomed by death coming from the sky, the peace of death
Wind from the East, a stench of death
Cafal thinks back to his conversation with Ganoes Paran years ago
A man possessing power must act decisively… else it trickle away through his fingers
Cafal thinks his words to Paran are naive. Now believes Paran’s indecision is not weakness, but rightfully cautious and wise
Tool’s authority as Warleader is weakening, nothing he nor Cafal can do to stop it
Cafal kicks awake Talamandas on the tent floor
Talamandas travels the warrens, speaks to the Barghast gods about wars, betrayals, alliances. They are stubborn for not working together with human gods against a mutual unspecified threat
The Barghast wanted to fight alongside the Grey Swords, their gods wanted to serve the Wolves. However when they came to Lether, the Grey Swords were dead.
Cafal knew Setoc was Letherii but all civilization was lost on her, the wild had reclaimed her and she is possibly a priestess and inheritor of the Wolves of Winter

Bottle thinks Smiles is pissed at him for using the stomachache excuse first to skip the war games
Corabb appears and spooks Bottle, who flings open the lockbox and points out it was actually Cuttle’s
Before Corabb beats up Bottle over a misunderstanding of a voice, Bottle leaves
Bottle realizes Quick Ben has been telepathically communicating with Bottle and tells him to meet him at the Cedance
Sinn and Grub are gone
Bottle is able to find the Cedance without QB’s directions
QB thinks the Ere’sal ‘furry lover’ guides Bottle with visions of her own memories
Bottle usually sees scenes of a frozen landscape, of jungles, cliffs with four-legged monkeys, the Eres’al huddling for warmth while predators surround them

The most memorable one was on a white coral beach that feels like home, and the Eres built boats and conquered the world until humans came. The Eres’al had explored the world first through their roads of the sea
At the Cedance, Quick Ben is surprised it and magic isn’t dying despite warrens and the Deck of Dragons brought over, and slamming the door on Chaos

Quick Ben’s talk of the Eres’al’s roads of the sea makes him think of Mael. QB is aware Mael’s been hiding beside Tehol, but is helpless when mortals like Mallick Rel grasps Mael’s power and “forced concessions”
[Spoiler Note: Mallick Rel assassinated Surly and is the new Malazan Emperor]
Bottle say Mael is a thirsty god, and his daughter Beru, Lady of Fair Seas, isn’t much better
QB wants Tavore to promote Bottle to High Mage, Bottle rejects that and persuades to keep him as QB’s “shaved knuckle in the hole”
Sandalath wants to leave with Withal, and join the Shake

Sandalath recalls the Saelen Gara, a Tiste Andii people that lived in the forests of Kurald Galain and chose to remain and die when their world died, despite Andarist’s plea for them to seek refuge in Kharkanas
Sandalath feels the same thing is happening with the Bonehunters marching to their deaths to Kolanse, Sandalath doesn’t want to witness an entire people die again
Sandalath and Withal discuss the Shake
After the war between the Tiste Edur and Tiste Andii versus the K’Chain Che’Malle, surviving Andii mixed with humans who would become the Shake
The Bluerose Tiste Andii wandered inland and remained pure in their worship of Anomander Rake
Deadsmell’s squad and Sinn found skeletons that were half human, half reptilian on the north end of the island
[Note: Over generations the Shake had been afflicted by genetic material of a desperate KCCM Matron spilled into the sea as they lost the war to the invading Tiste Edur]
Withal asks why they warred in the first place, Sandalath answers because they are different
Sandalath doesn’t answer when asked if it was because they were the invaders
Telorast & Curdle are messing with Banaschar as he’s passed out drunk
They want revenge against the Errant for ‘stealing’ their pet Banaschar
Banaschar wakes and says the Errant wants power, worshipers, and domination. He will nudge and manipulate the coming war over the Crippled God to take down the gods and the High Houses
Banaschar continues to struggle with being the last survivor of the D’rek cult. Wonders if D’rek has forgotten him, or if it’s a matter of time when she finds and kills him too
Telorast & Curdle go find another bottle for Banaschar
War games between the Bonehunters and the Letherii army
Smiles and Koryk stalk a Letherii scout
They believe the Letherii still hold to traditional clashes on open fields, with scouts sent ahead for reconnaissance
The Malazans use tactics including splitting forces, avoid direct clashes, and whittling down armies with raids, ambushes, and disrupting supply chains.
The Tiste Edur had similar tactics and defeated the Letherii at once
The war games are to help prepare the Letherii against the imperial Malazan Army if they come to conquer
Smiles returns to the Malazan camp, Gullstream greets her
Gullstream has dark skin, with a pink blotch on half his face and most of his forehead. He has almond-shaped eyes that keep changing colors. He’s rumored to be part Tiste Andii and well hung
Smiles walks past Gullstream and reports the Letherii scout to Fist Keneb, Sgt. Fiddler, and Sgt. Balm
Fiddler knows Brys sent five pairs of scouts. The Letherii scout wanted to be seen while his partner remains hidden
Fist Keneb orders Sgt. Balm to retrieve a map, but Balm doesn’t know about a map so Keneb goes over to Reliko
Reliko and Vastly Blank joined Drawfirst and Shoaly under Sgt. Primly because his original sergeant, Badan Gruk, called out sick from the war games along with Sgt. Sinter and Kisswhere
Keneb orders Reliko to get the map
Sgt. Fiddler says Keneb could’ve been done by now if Keneb went himself, for talking back Keneb orders Fiddler to get the table
Keneb asks why the heavies are looking at their hands
Reliko says they’re counting their lost fingers, rumored that Nefarias Bredd in Fist Blistig’s legion lost both thumbs
Smiles muses that kingdoms are toppled by dumb soldiers like them
(Smiles)
Smiles returns to Koryk with Cpl. Tarr following behind
The Letherii successfully deceived the Bonehunter soldiers
(Keneb)
The Letherii ambushes Fist Keneb’s troops with non-lethal arrows, Brys Beddict walks up to Keneb and paints a red slash across his armor
Keneb says well done, but the lesson is that the Bonehunters are willing to lose 300 men in exchange for 800 Letherii and their supreme commander, as the Letherii are surrounded on all sides
Keneb also says to listen to their veterans regardless of rank, the Bonehunters’ victory is thanks to Fiddler who wants two nights off for his squad
Keneb could’ve drawn the battle out but would rather sleep in a comfy bed so he willingly walked into the ambush so they could return to Letheras
(Sort)
Cpt. Faradan Sort walks into Cpt. Kindly’s office to find him staring at a pile of animal hair on his desk
Kindly suspects Lt. Pores, Sort suggests crushing what he loves under their heel to take care of troublemakers (recalling the scorpion)
Sort wants to find their two wayward mages including High Mage Sinn because she saved them in Y’Ghatan and Tavore desperately needs mages on their journey across Kolanse
Sort leaves to find Quick Ben to help in the search
(Sinter)
Sgt. Sinter, Kisswhere, and Sgt. Badan Gruk play a Dal Honese version of bones [Note: think ancient dominoes]. Everyone is cheating but accuse the other
Sinter speculates the bones were from Li Heng thieves that were punished. Observes how things were less fun when civilized society outlawed such torture and barbaric punishments
‘A state that employs torture invites barbarism and deserves nothing better than to suffer the harvest of its own excesses’, Kellanved when he took over
Lt. Pores walks up failing and insisting to be Cpt. Kindly. Orders the two women to grow out their hair and lose weight, showing up in their undergarments to Kindly’s office to prove it
Lt. Pores walks away, Sinter wants Badan Gruk to go find two fat and ugly prostitutes to prank Pores
Withal asks Sandalath about a woman’s response, gets a cryptic reply
Sandalath asks why the nachts are with them
Withal said he prayed to Mael on the Crippled God’s island and now they follow him
Sandalath wants to leave the Malazans and Letheras that night
(Grub)
Grub and Sinn explore a ‘new’ warren they entered through the dead Azath Tower
Windy desert, straight road of rock and glass, stone ruins of old homes, burnt carriages and corpses on the road
Grub is concerned about water, food, shelter, fire
Sinn cryptically responds that what is real is different to individuals.

Sinn talks about her Tanno Spiritwalker tutor, they believe untethered souls drown in wisdom. Souls are tethered to beliefs, knowledge is poison, souls become more wise when they sever their beliefs and consequently drown
The last thing that was real to the people that died here was fire
(Sinn)
Grub and Sinn watch as they’re surrounded by ghosts, the land’s memories of an army
Horse chariots, wagons, dark skinned warriors in bronze armor
A ghost priest senses Grub and Sinn, approaching and blindly reaches his arms out touching their heads
Sinn wants to let him, to believe they are a divinity to shatter their ‘sanctuary of ignorance’ with knowledge
The ghost priest wails, turns back to his army and king. The ghost army flees
Ghost slaves appear to raise a cairn and place offerings of food upon it
‘Divine gifts, [Sinn said], were not gifts at all. The receiver must pay for them.’
The Errant walks into a chamber, Sechul Lath/Knuckles follows
Sechul Lath’s mother Kilmandaros has woken up, trapped in Sechul’s bone offerings of chance
Sechul Lath, Lord of the Hold of Chance, the Toppler, the Conniver, the Wastrel of Ruin
The Errant kicks over the bone offerings, Kilmandaros is frightened. The Errant came to talk about dragons

Gunth Mach’s body changes, her spikes flattened and hide forming a saddle for Kalyth to ride as a steed
Kalyth rides Gunth, flanked by K’ell Hunters Rythok and Kor Thuran, Sag’Churok scouts a league ahead leading them east then veering south
The group come upon an ancient battlefield with the bones of dragons
Kalyth feels the KCCM expect something from her as their Destriant, but she has no knowledge of their history to think of anything
Kalyth picks up a sun bleached dragon tooth, big as a club in her hands. But this one isn’t important, she sees a rust colored otataral tooth embedded in a dragon skull
Sag’Churok speaks to her. The otararal makes it difficult to hold their telepathic connection
The KCCM believe there cannot be a single god. A single god means everything is in order without chaos. If everything is predetermined, then everything has no meaning or value

The KCCM believe mortal knowledge of magic is flawed. Mortals ‘cut the veins of other worlds and drink of the blood, and this is your sorcery.’ The KCCM believe all life is sorcery, to kill life is to kill magic. When KCCM kill, they weep with compassion for the life and magic they killed
Otataral is the opposite of magic, negation to creation, absence to presence, death to life.
The Otataral Dragon has been bound, entities are seeking to release and control it. The KCCM worship the god of life
(Kalyth)
Gunth Mach has Kalyth inhale the KCCM’s breath, Kalyth is transported to where the Otataral Dragon is crucified
If the Otataral Dragon is freed, the “other” god of life may also return and thus the forces in opposition engage in their eternal battle again
Kalyth draws a conclusion as Destriant
The KCCM should find their faith in each other, not the gods who war above them. Faith that is absolute loyalty to each other with humility and without arrogance.
Find people who whose sacrifice will be made in the name of compassion, the only cause worth fighting and dying for
Kalyth is resolved to find these champions
(Sag’Churok)
Kalyth leads the KCCM. Sag’Churok an Gunth Mach feels pride in their Destriant
Characters
Setoc, Letherii wolf-girl
Cafal, Great Barghast Warlock and Hetan’s brother
Torrent, the last Awl that Toc saved
Talamandas, sticksnare
A wagon carries the Barghast corpses of the Gadra clan scouts [killed by Kalyth’s KCCM in Chapter 4]
The Gadra clan are bloodthirsty, blindly swearing vengeance on the Akrynnai, D'rhasilhani, and Letherii
Gadra Warchief Stolmen can’t stop his people, or else be deposed
Cafal plans to leave, frustrated the clan want to wage war against the Akrynnai who have done nothing
Torrent wants to find Tool for permission to leave the Barghast, and beg for forgiveness in not taking Toc’s place in death. Cafal attempts to console Torrent’s guilt
Cafal offers to open a warren to travel to Tool faster
Setoc is against it, the warrens are weak in Letheras and the Barghast gods are not ready
Talamandas takes offense, argues with Setoc
Setoc believes the Gadra clan’s senseless violence will have the rest of the Letheras peoples against them: Akrynnai, D'rhasilhani, Keryn, Saphinand, and Bolkando
Gadra Warchief Stolmen’s wife Sekara comes out of her tent to berate Setoc and declare other Letheras peoples are invaders, not the Barghast who lost their home here thousands of years ago
The barghast women hate Setoc for drawing attention from the men, Setoc smirks at Stolmen and he has to hold his wife back from attacking her. The commotion draws a mob of people around them
Cafal and Talamandas open a warren to get the group out of there against Setoc’s warning. White fire blinds and concusses the group, transporting them to a stone barrow in another world
Talamandas is destroyed ☠
Cafal and Talamandas knew of the poison in the warrens and prepared wards against it, something else caused the white fire
Setoc finds a coin, Cafal’s clan makes armor out of coins but doesn’t recognize this one in particular
One side has an empress, the other side has crossed swords. Looks likes Seven Cities but wrong writing, hint its of a different world
Cafal follows where the bats group up and find a hole in the wall, they remove bricks and rush outside into a dark forest as the barrow collapses
Setoc senses all of the wolves in the area had been hunted centuries ago
Cafal wants Setoc’s help to summon the ghost wolves to aid him in sanctifying the group and use it to get them home. Offer to take them to their world where they can join living wolves
Setoc calls out, hundreds of thousands of wolves killed by spears, snares, traps, and infection appear. Other animals likestas, bhederin, and large cats also appear
Setoc sees a small portal and calls the animals loved ones, asking to make the portal bigger
Taxilian leads the group away from the room with the sacrificed KCCM, through really scif looking hallways of metal cables and tubes, some ripped open and spilling puddles of oil
Taxilian, Rautos, Breath, Sheb, Nappet, Last, Asane

The group reaches a huge 8-walled chamber outlined by ledges. They can’t see the floor or ceiling, the center of the chamber has x8 brass and iron machine cylinders the size of city towers, some levels with balconies
Rautos believes they’re looking at pressure chambers
The Ghost follows Taxilian’s group and lore dumps to themself
The ‘city’ is a skykeep named Kalse Rooted
A Shi'Gal had killed the K’ell Hunters at the entrance to seal the failure of the fortress
J’an Sentinels had taken their Matron to entomb her in the battlegrounds
Asane wants to die to escape her aging mind and body
Last recalls a childhood memory, crying because he crushed a nest of mice while he dismantled a shed. His dad took them to their daily visits to his mother’s graves, happy to see Last finally crying

Sheb recalled being sent to jail after Hivanar agents accused him of embezzling, being sent to work the lime pits for 10 years, planning on stealing the rest of Xaranthos Hivanar’s wealth and blackmailing him
Nappet fantasizes about raping Sheb and recalling how he killed his sister’s abusive husband and was sentenced to labor at a quarry near Bluerose

Breath fears being raped by Sheb and Nappet, thinking about ways to kill him. Breath recalls a story about [Feather Witch], how she was raped by other men, and tragically could’ve foreseen a happy future with [Udinaas] if she had been aware of her gift with Tiles sooner
Rautos does not recall his family name, thinks about the loveless marriage with his wife, both pursuing potential, both searching for love elsewhere
(Ghost)

Taxilian thinks about his machines. The machine city they find themselves in. Machines that would travel faster than horses or ships, machines that could preserve human souls after the death of the body, machines to end hunger, poverty, avarice, cruelty, inequity, etc.
Mortals are flawed in their moral constructs as they can’t hold themselves to the standards they impose on others, machines of morality would end all intelligent life due to their flaws
Taxilian wants to find such a moral machine in the KCCM skykeep, the slaughter of the KCCM they found was evidence it existed here
(Ghost)
The Ghost is horrified by Taxilian’s thoughts
‘Justice without compassion was the destroyer of morality, a slayer blind to empathy.’
The ghost believes nature is a force that will find balance, the process belonging only to time
The ghost realizes he has a thing about ‘time’
(Taxilian)

Taxilian’s group passes through vats of fungi and plants that need no light, vats with nests of orthen scaled rats, living dorms, manufacturing plants, armories of weapons, warehouses of foodstuffs, ice rooms with frozen meat on hooks, etc.
Taxilian continues walking forward as if possessed
The ex-prisoners of the Second Maiden Fort prison islands started rioting after they learned Yan Tovis plans to take them to an unknown world with no sun
The Maiden Fort islanders don’t want to be lost in a sunless world if Yan Tovis fails
Murder, rape, arson
Only a few thousand of the ten thousand Maiden Fort islanders take refuge with the Shake
Yedan Derryg leads a troop of 30+ Letherii soldiers, to protect Yan Tovis while she opens the Road to Gallan. She reluctantly agrees
Yedan’s troop, Pithy, and Brevity are tasked to protect the islander refugees
Yan Tovis goes to Skwish & Pully on top of a shell midden/heap
Yan Tovis cuts her arms to offer her blood, the two witches grab her arms and scream the Words of Sundering. A portal opens on the water
Yan Tovis goes into the portal, screaming to herself in grief
The ex-prisoners pause as the portal is summoned and watch as the Shake and refugee Maiden Fort islanders all escape into the portal
The ex-prisoners attack Yedan Derryg’s troop with Pithy and Brevity holding the line.
A Letherii soldier gets stabbed in the thigh, two of Brevity’s guard pull him back and control his bleeding
Pithy and Brevity loot the ex-prisoner weapons to bolster their rearguard, a tactic that annoys Yedan Derryg
Yedan’s troops are tiring fast, haven’t had enough practice since the Edur invasion [Note: Midnight Tides]
Yedan’s line retreats momentarily, them bounces back fiercely to slaughter the ex-prisoners, breaking their morale forcing them to abandon their weapons and flee
The fighting ends
The wounded are attended to
Pithy and Brevity said Yedan would be the best commander the Shake could have
Yedan Derryg walks into the portal

i.html: Badalle, Rutt holding Held, Brayderal, and Saddic travelled across the plains with jade streaks in the sky as more children died
Some collapsed during the journey
Some died after drinking bright green water possibly contaminated and tasted like limestone
Opals, carrion beetles that followed alongside the children
Diamonds, lizards that drank blood from fingertips and turned ruby red
Shards, locusts that eat the children, leaving red stained bones behind
Brayderal is a tall girl that reminds Badalle of the Quitters, Badall does not trust her
Saddic has a crush on Badalle, has a book to record all her poems
Badalle tells Saddic a poem he can record but only on an empty page
Saddic falls asleep at Badalle’s side, Badalle thinks about eating Saddic’s arms

King Tehol, Bugg, Queen Janath, and Shurq Elalle have a meal together
Janath and Shurq fake argue over Tehol, making him nervous to flee the conversation with Bugg
When Tehol and Bugg leave, Janath tells Shurq about people that need Shurq’s ship
Janath wants to eliminate temptations from Tehol, Shurq suggests to live in excess and would not want to be revived from one of the Malazan necromancers because she enjoys unending pleasure
(Bugg)
Tehol and Bugg leave, aware Janath is scheming something with Shurq
Bugg says court plots and schemes are necessary, healthy even
(Shurq Elalle)
Princess Felash (14th daughter of King Tarkulf of Bolkando) and her handmaiden enter the dining room as Janath’s guests to speak with Shurq Elalle

Felash is plump wearing tight clothing, gaudy jewelry, and spike heeled shoes. Dark eyeliner, glittery purple eyeshadow, pink and amber lip gloss, white foundation, pink blush. Silky black hair braided and held with pearl-tipped porcupine quills
The handmaiden is a buff woman with a pink embroidered gown, diamonds studded on her cheeks, and blonde super short hair
Princess Felash was sent by her mother Queen Abrastal on a secret mission to deliver “assurances” that would prevent war if the Malazans “enter a viper’s nest”
The handmaiden gives bombastic side eyes to everyone during the conversation
Felash is aware Shurq is a pirate and can accommodate her
Shurq demands a contract to be paid well, Felash agrees
(Shurq Elalle)
Shurq and Janath speak after Felash and her handmaiden leaves
Janath compares the Bolkando scheming factions to a neighborhood sandbox/cat litter box where children fight and throw cat scat at each other
Janath says Felash is 14 years old and came to eliminate Bugg’s rival spy networks
Shurq isn’t looking forward to escorting Felash to the Akrynnai Range
(Harbro, Felash)
Princess Felash and her handmaiden are escorted by Janath’s servants through hidden passages to the postern gate where a carriage awaits to deliver them to their harborfront hostel
Felash is unsure about Shurq Elalle and ready to kill her with her dagger if need be
The handmaiden says she can’t die because an ootooloo keeps her undead
(Letheras, Bugg)
Tehol and Bugg are joined by Janath and Shurq outside in the night air
Deadsmell stands by the Azath Tower, thinks about his home village Gethran, 30 leagues north of Li Heng in Quon Tali

At 17 years old, Deadsmell had taken up gravekeeper duties after the previous gravekeeper Old Scez was killed by a husband. Old Scez has slept with a lot of the women in the village, possibly including Deadsmell’s mom while his dad was fighting in the Quon Tali civil war

The cemetery had three tiers dividing the social classes. The upper level had sepulchres like mini cathedrals for the wealthy. The middle tier had modest burials for the not so middle but surviving middle class. The bottom tier were pits for the addicts, criminals, and drunks periodically turned over like compost heaps
At 19 years old, Deadsmell had witnessed the Fener priest Hester Vill pass away from a stroke at nearly a hundred years old. The fireplace burned with no fuel, Hood had come to collect

Hood feels that Deadsmell is one of his own and engages in a game of evasion, a form of worship. As a necromancer, Deadsmell can take lives out of Hood’s reach, cheating death as much as possible. Deadsmell must respect that he will lose every single time, in exchange Hood must respect Deadsmell for his courage to try, for stubborn refusal is a mortal’s greatest strength. Deadsmell will be gifted the end of fear, accepting death as part of life

Deadsmell begs for Hood not to be cruel with Hester, Hood says he’s not one to be cruel but can’t help that Hester’s soul is abused. Deadsmell says Fener will pay for that, Hood is amused and says the gods will answer to death
‘There is no bargain when only one side pays attention’
Deadsmell thinks about Hood’s words and thinks about how Brys Beddict and [Shurq Elalle] were brought back from the dead
Bottle arrives, Deadsmell had sent Crump as the messenger to meet at the Azath House
Deadsmell sent cattledog Bent and lapdog Roach to track down Sinn and Grub into the Azath House
Deadsmell figures the kids and the dogs won’t return, already told Adjunct Tavore
Bottle could’ve rode one of the animals souls and see where they went, Deadsmell admits he fucked up
Deadsmell asks Bottle what he sees when he looks into the Eres’al’s eyes when she visits
Bottle sees so much ‘need’, and eyes only in the present without regard for last or future
Deadsmell says that Hood’s eyes may be the same as the Eres’al’s, full and empty, that there is absence in them. Eyes when their soul has left
Deadsmell feels he is out of moves
Sgt. Hellian says she isn’t into fingering Skulldeath’s bumhole when she falls down the gap between the mattresses on the floor
Hellian suddenly has a childhood memory of holding a dead minnow, she doesn’t remember where she grew up or who she is. She blames Skulldeath for feeling sober
Hellian calls him a bastard, Skulldeath says he’s a prince and will make Hellian his Queen
Hellian says she never knelt to anybody and won’t make anybody kneel to her, laughs that Skulldeath is only a soldier, and vomits
Cuttle and Sgt. Fiddler watch over the Malazan camps outside Letheras, campfires and tents
Cuttle recounts their army crossing Seven Cities to put down the Whirlwind Rebellion, Y’Ghatan, then crossing the ocean to put down the Tiste Edur empire for attacking the Malazan Empire
After all that, Cuttle still feels anxiety about their next destination for an unknown purpose
They’re not mercenaries for hire
Rescuing allies, Khundryl Burned Tears and Perish Grey Helms fighting in Bolkando, is not the reason they’re on Lether in the first place
Cuttle compares the Bonehunters to the Bridgeburners for Fiddler
Cuttle asks why Fiddler has a problem with Hedge now that he’s back
Fiddler accepted that Hedge and his friends are dead, can’t reconcile him being alive again. Reminds him of his dead friends, and that he’ll end up alone again
Cuttle and Fiddler enter the sick area, 200 cots all occupied by sick soldiers
All Denul healers are exhausted
Only Malazan casualties, possible contagions in leaking latrines, standing water, soiled food from experience as a sapper
Fiddler decides to find Brys Beddict
(Tarr)
Cpl. Tarr repairs his chain hauberk, Smiles interrupts to annoy him
Corabb arrives with a new Letherii sword he carefully carries after breaking his weapon
Smiles makes fun of him, Tarr sends her away so Corabb can excitedly look at his new weapon
(Smiles)
Smiles wanders, thinking Koryk would be decent company if he weren’t sick
Finds Mayfly, Tulip, Flashwit, Shortnose, Saltlick, Drawfirst, Lookback, and Vastly Blank staring at a footprint they think is from Nefarias Bredd
Smiles offers to play bones, invites Vastly Blank to be next to her
(Pores)
Cpt. Kindly takes Lt. Pores to the parade square where 12 Letherii new recruits await
Two are obese prostitutes that Sgt. Badan Gruk found after Pores (badly pretending to be Kindly) ordered Sinter and Kisswhere to lose weight and show up to Kindly’s office in their underwear
Kindly promotes Pores to Master Sergeant in charge of the new recruits
Master Sgt. Pores promotes a moustached man to squad leader and names him Twit. Orders the dozen recruits to vomit and get their new uniform and kit
(Pores)
Master Sgt. Pores assigns the new recruits to Sgt. Badan Gruk’s, Sgt. Sinter’s, and Sgt. Primly’s squads [Note; for pranking him]
Sgt. Twit, Sgt. Nose Stream, Cpl. Rumjugs, Cpl. Sweetlard
(Pores)
Pores commandeers (steals) a tent in Sgt. Urb’s squad, bribes the soldiers with the promise of vintage wine, and goes inside to drink alcohol he stole from the new recruits
(Kisswhere)
Kisswhere and Sgt. Pravalak Rim help Rumjugs and Sweetlard set up their tents
Kisswhere leaves to get Skulldeath
(Twit not Sunrise)
Sgt. Twit talks about how he doesn’t like his name
Ruffle advises Twit to pretend to drown and come back as his twin brother and encourages him to make up a story
Twit comes up with a story about losing his money from failed construction investments, his wife leaving him, deciding to join the Malazan army since King Tehol doesn’t look like warmonger
Ruffle renames him Sgt. Sunrise
Sgt. Fiddler and Cuttle find Brys Beddict looking over the bridge canal and tells him about the mosquito ague
Brys knows it as the Shivers and its treatment, water from Bugg’s mill pump that draws up water with bubbles and a tart taste. Brys sends 500 casks and his military healers
Fiddler mentions from experience usually locals get sick when foreigners arrive, but this was the opposite
Brys comments on imperial expansion, encroaching on territory slowly until tribes stand up for themselves, and empires come up with lies about “defending themselves” to conquer
Fiddler recalls a story about a remote Strike Island, visiting them under Admiral Nok during Emperor Kellanved’s reign.

The chief had 200 warriors compared to Nok’s fleet of 5000 marines. The chief hoped to gift his entire wealth of trinkets on the beach in hopes the Malazans took it and left, Admiral Nok in turn gifted them a golden throne along with wool and silk clothing, giving them private time to sort and distribute the gifts

Intentional or not, the village was sick from a contagion that wiped out a third of its people. Fiddler wonders if the chief cursed the Malazans upon his dying breath. The Malazans’ noble intentions meant nothing
Brys comments the Letheras River collects silts in the ground, sending them to the bottom of the ocean
Cuttle cynically jokes he’ll jump off the bridge if he keeps listening to them
Fiddler tells Cuttle optimism is worthless and evil if it ignores others’ suffering. Pessimism is the first step to honest fighting against suffering. Brys adds that it’s a heroic path
Brys thanks Fiddler before leaving
Fiddler thinks what he said convinces Cuttle to stop looking up to him and also leaves
Cuttle shakes his head and follows Fiddler
Kalyth recalls the Elan people’s custom of having a clay figure bound to each person. Kalyth feels shame for having lost hers
Kalyth recalls a bhederin bull that remained standing as it was stabbed by 15 javelins, its last stand of defiance. She feels similar to that bhederin as the last of her people

Aramala and Cynnigig are Jaghut that fought alongside the T’lan Imass to defeat Jaghut Tyrants. After, the Imass had betrayed the Jaghut committed to their genocide. A group of 8 T’lan Imass scouts had found Aramala in her tower, Aramala killed seven of them while the eighth scout fled and returned with an T’lan Imass army who pinned her with a rock and sealed her with Tellann. The seven scouts that died were entombed in darkness for their failure.

Overtime, they became worshiped by the Teblor as the Seven Faces in the Rock. The Seven had sworn fealty to the Crippled God in exchange for breaking the Vow Ritual of Tellann and became the Unbound. They had cultivated their Teblor worshipers and ultimately led to following Karsa Orlong as spirits. Following him onto the Silanda to a dreamworld within barrow mounds that leads to the realm of Omtose Phellack.

Karsa follows the trail of the T’lan Imass army and exits the Omtose Phellack Warren into the Jhag Odhan. Here, Karsa finds a flint quarry containing a network of caves holding a cache of Imass flint weapons. The Unbound arriving to their cache of weapons was the last task to free them from the Vow. The Unbound aid Karsa in making his own flint sword and imbuing it with the Ritual of Tellann to make it indestructible. Karsa was offered to be the eighth member of the Unbound, the souls of sacrificed Teblor children as his army, and the position of Knight of Chains. Instead Karsa destroys Sinballe and tells them to fuck off, never touch the Teblor again. Karsa grants Sinballe oblivion by throwing her skull into the ocean.

(in the Bonehunters) Five of the Unbound came to Barathol Mekhar’s village at the Tapur Crossroads. Months later Heboric, Greyfrog, Scillara, Crokus, and Felisin Younger came to the village. The Unbound attacked them and kidnapped Felisin Younger to bring to the city of the fallen, Hanar Ara. Kulat, a seneschal of the Crippled God, has prepared the city for her and proclaimed her Sha’ik Reborn. Those broken and crippled by Poliel’s plague came to populate the city. However, Felisin the Younger disbands the Rebel army and abandons the Book of Dryjhna to start a new book of Salvation.

The Errant uses his power as Master of the Tiles to summon the Elder Gods. The only ones who respond are Sechul Lath, Kilmandaros, Mael, and Olar Ethil. The Errant wants to revive the ancient glory and power of the Elder Gods

The Bonehunters march with the Letherii Army to the Wastelands, planning to go to the Kolanse Kingdoms where they can find the heart of the Crippled God and free him. Approaching the Wastelands they were caught in the wrong place, wrong time. The K’Chain Nah’Ruk came to war against the K’Chain Che’Malle and the Bonehunters were defeated

Onos Toolan was leader of the White Face Barghast trying to avoid facing an ancient enemy. The Barghast hated Tool for being against their culture, killing Tool and hobbling his wife Hetan. With nudges from Olar Ethil, Tool was resurrected as a T’lan Imass and proceeded to slaughter his own Barghast Senan clan
Olar Ethil continued to manipulate Tool to force him to be her First Sword of her army, even using Toc the Younger to prevent him from saving his family.
The White Face Barghast warred against the resident Akrynnai traders
Both the Barghast and Akrynnai were destroyed as Draconus was released from Dragnipur and descends onto the Lether continent

Yan Tovis had shed her blood to open a gate that led the Shake people and Maiden Islander refugees back to Kharkanas. Yedan Derryg retraced Shake legends to find a Hust sword along the First Shore. Sandalath Drukorlat, a former noble hostage in Kharkanas, and her lover Withal come to Kharkanas and Sandalath is still struggling whether or not to embrace them as Queen

Kalyth is the Destriant of the Gunth Mach, a new K’Chain Che’Malle Matron. Her Shi’Gal, named Gu’Rull, went out searching for a Mortal Sword and Shield Anvil and retrieved Gesler and Stormy because they were bright like beacons.

The K’Chain Nah’Ruk were a species of “short-tailed” K’Chain that the Che-Malle “long-tails” had revived to create a slave workforce. That did not go well, as they rose up in civil war. The Nah’Ruk sought to annihilate the Che’Malle, and are thought to own the Imperial Warren.
Despite being dinosaurs that operate giant flying fortresses that shoots lightning, they never fought with tactics. Having Gesler and Stormy gave them the edge to defeat the K’Chain Nah’Ruk.

Icarium had activated his machine underneath Letheras to create new warrens, stealing the souls of several people including Feather Witch, Rautos Hivanar, and Taralack Veed. He ended up exploring Kalse Rooted, a K’Chain Che’Malle skykeep that didn’t need a matron because it specifically belonged to him. Once Icarium awakened and took his throne, he joined the K’Chain Che’Malle fight against the K’Chain Nah’Ruk, buried Kalse Rooted into the hole in the sky warren, and activated the Errant’s Eye, given to him by Feahter Witch, as a Finnest to form an Azath that sealed the Nah’Ruk’s hole in the sky, preventing more Gath’Ran Citadels from invading the world.

Grub and Sinn went through the Dead Azath Tower in Letheras to explore Icarium’s new warrens and ended up showing up at the end to help the K’Chain Che’Malle and Icarium’s Kalse Rooted to fight back against the K’Chain Nah’Ruk

The Snake are orphaned children from all over Kolanse and the Elan plains after the Forkrul Assail came and conquered. The Snake were being chased by a handful of Forkrul Assail until they were destroyed by Badalle using her own Voice. They arrive at the crystal city of Icarius, previously created by Icarium.

Setoc is a Letherii girl whose family was killed by Redmask. She became the Destriant to the Wolves of Winter and lived among the Barghast. She left the barghast after the civil war, ended up taking in Tool and Hetan’s children Stavi, Storii, and Absi as well as running into the Trygalle Trade Guild that arrived from Hood’s realm including Mappo, Gruntle, the Cartographer, and some Shareholders
